'''Muhammad Suhail Zubairy''' (born 19 October 1952)<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences">{{cite web|title=Fellow - M. Suhail. Zubairy profile|url=http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=170|publisher=Pakistan Academy of Sciences website|access-date=18 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140917203552/http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=170|archive-date=17 September 2014}}</ref> is a Pakistani-American physicist and a Distinguished Professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at [[Texas A&M University]], where he holds the [[Charles Munnerlyn#Career|Munnerlyn-Heep Chair in Quantum Optics]]. He is known for his contributions to quantum optics, quantum informatics, quantum entanglement, and sub-wavelength lithography.<ref>{{Citation| url = http://www.science.tamu.edu/news/story.php?story_ID=1181#.U9NoLGPLIyg/|title = Quantum Physicist Suhail Zubairy Appointed University Distinguished Professor| access-date =18 October 2022| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170222025522/http://www.science.tamu.edu/news/story.php?story_ID=1181#.U9NoLGPLIyg/|archive-date = 22 February 2017|website=Texas A&M University website}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Zubairy was born in [[Lahore]], Pakistan. He attended [[Edwardes College]] in Peshawar, where he received double BSc degree in [[physics]] and mathematics from the [[Peshawar University]], in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Muhammad Suhail Zubairy |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview/1125591/prof-dr-muhammad-suhail-zubairy |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de |language=en}}</ref> He received MSc in physics from the [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] in 1974, and his PhD in physics from the [[University of Rochester]] under the guidance of [[Emil Wolf]] in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web
  | title =M. Suhail Zubairy
  | publisher =[[Texas A&M University]], Department of Physics & Astronomy website
  | url =http://www.physics.tamu.edu/people/showpeople.php?name=M.%20Suhail%20Zubairy&userid=zubairy
  | access-date =18 October 2022
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110720054807/http://physics.tamu.edu/people/showpeople.php?name=M.%20Suhail%20Zubairy&userid=zubairy
  | archive-date =20 July 2011
  }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Zubairy was born in [[Lahore, Pakistan]]. He attended [[Edwardes College Peshawar|Edwardes College]] in Peshawar, where he received a double BSc degree in physics and mathematics from the [[University of Peshawar]] in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guindi |first=Abigail |title=The Man Who Made The Quantum World Make Sense |url=https://artsci.tamu.edu/news/2026/05/the-man-who-made-the-quantum-world-make-sense.html |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=artsci.tamu.edu |language=en}}</ref> He earned an MSc in physics from [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] in 1974 and a PhD in physics from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1978 under the supervision of [[Emil Wolf]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Wolf |first=Emil |title=Introduction to the Theory of Coherence and Polarization of Light |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-521-82035-6}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1978 to 1979, Zubairy was a research associate at the University of Rochester. He then held a research associate position at the Optical Sciences Center, [[University of Arizona]] (1979–1980), followed by a role as research assistant professor at the [[University of New Mexico]] (1980–1984).<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences" />

In 1984, he joined the Department of Electronics at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad, as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 1985 and to professor in 1992, remaining there until 2004.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book
  | last =Zubairy
  | first =M. Suhail
  |author2=Marlan Scully
  |author2-link=Marlan Scully
  | title =Quantum Optics
  | publisher =Cambridge University Press
  | year =1997
  | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=20ISsQCKKmQC&q=Muhammad+Suhail+Zubairy+Quantum+Optics| isbn =0-521-43595-1
}}</ref>

In 2004, Zubairy moved to Texas A&M University as a professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy. He was appointed Munnerlyn-Heep Chair in Quantum Optics in 2010 and named University Distinguished Professor in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-14 |title=Sarah Zubairy |url=https://cepr.org/about/people/sarah-zubairy |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=CEPR |language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, he was awarded the Changjiang Distinguished Chair Professorship at Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan, China.<ref name="phys.hust.edu.cn">{{Citation| url =http://phys.hust.edu.cn/xsdt/1606.htm| title = Changjiang Distinguished Chair Professor|website=Huazhong University of Science and Technology School of Physics website| access-date =18 October 2022|archive-date =16 April 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170416220834/http://phys.hust.edu.cn/xsdt/1606.htm}}</ref>

His recent ''[[Physical Review Letters]]''<ref>{{Citation

==Research==
Zubairy's research has focused on theoretical quantum optics, quantum coherence, quantum entanglement, quantum information science, and quantum metrology.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Scully |first1=Marlan O. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=20ISsQCKKmQC |title=Quantum Optics |last2=Zubairy |first2=M. Suhail |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1997 |isbn=978-0-521-43595-6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liao |first1=Zeyang |last2=Al-Amri |first2=M. |last3=Suhail Zubairy |first3=M. |date=2010-10-25 |title=Quantum Lithography beyond the Diffraction Limit via Rabi Oscillations |url=https://physics.aps.org/synopsis-for/10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.183601 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en-US |volume=105 |issue=18 |article-number=183601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.183601 |pmid=21231103 |bibcode=2010PhRvL.105r3601L |issn=0031-9007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407233529/https://physics.aps.org/synopsis-for/10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.183601 |archive-date=2017-04-07}}</ref>

=== Quantum optics and laser physics ===
Zubairy contributed to the theory of squeezed states, [[atomic coherence]], and quantum-noise reduction in laser systems.<ref name=":0" /> His work on correlated-emission lasers and quantum-beat lasers examined mechanisms through which atomic coherence can suppress phase fluctuations and reduce quantum noise in optical systems.<ref name=":0" />

With physicist [[Marlan Scully]], Zubairy co-authored ''Quantum Optics'' (1997).<ref name=":0" />

=== Quantum entanglement ===
In collaboration with Mark Hillery, Zubairy developed entanglement criteria for optical systems. Their 2006 paper in ''Physical Review Letters'' introduced what became known as the Hillery–Zubairy criterion, a set of inequalities for detecting quantum entanglement in two-mode systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hillery |first1=Mark |last2=Zubairy |first2=M. Suhail |year=2006 |title=Entanglement Conditions for Two-Mode States |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.050503 |journal= Physical Review Letters|volume=96 |issue=5 |article-number=050503 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.050503|pmid=16486912 |arxiv=quant-ph/0507168 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..96e0503H }}</ref>

He also investigated the generation of macroscopic entangled states using correlated-emission laser systems and other quantum-optical platforms.<ref name=":0" />

=== Sub-wavelength lithography ===
Zubairy has proposed several theoretical schemes for achieving optical lithography beyond the classical diffraction limit. In the mid-2000s he and collaborators developed methods for sub-wavelength pattern formation using multi-photon interference and atomic coherence effects.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kapale |first1=Kishore T. |last2=Dowling |first2=Jonathan P. |last3=Zubairy |first3=M. Suhail |year=2005 |title=Quantum Lithography with Classical Light |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.163603 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=96 |issue=16 |article-number=163603 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.163603 |pmid=16712229 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Subsequent work introduced resonant and interferometric approaches to sub-wavelength lithography as well as schemes employing Rabi oscillations for nanoscale pattern generation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Liao |first1=Z. |last2=Zubairy |first2=M. Suhail |year=2010 |title=Quantum Lithography via Rabi Oscillations |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.183601 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=105 |issue=18 |article-number=183601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.183601 |pmid=21231103 |bibcode=2010PhRvL.105r3601L }}</ref>

=== Counterfactual quantum communication ===
In 2013, Zubairy and collaborators proposed a protocol for direct counterfactual quantum communication based on the chained quantum Zeno effect. The protocol was designed to enable information transfer between two parties without any information-carrying particles travelling through the transmission channel.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Salih |first1=Hatim |last2=Li |first2=Zheng-Hong |last3=Al-Amri |first3=M. |last4=Zubairy |first4=M. Suhail |year=2013 |title=Protocol for Direct Counterfactual Quantum Communication |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=110 |issue=17 |article-number=170502 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.170502|pmid=23679694 |arxiv=1206.2042 |bibcode=2013PhRvL.110q0502S }}</ref>

The proposal generated discussion concerning the foundations of quantum mechanics and the interpretation of counterfactual communication protocols.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Salih |first1=Hatim |last2=Li |first2=Zheng-Hong |last3=Al-Amri |first3=M. |last4=Zubairy |first4=M. Suhail |year=2014 |title=Reply to "Comment on Protocol for Direct Counterfactual Quantum Communication" |journal=Quantum Physics |arxiv=1404.5392 }}</ref>
